channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Reiner Pope – The math behind how LLMs are trained and served
item.description: Reiner Pope explores the underlying mathematical principles that govern the training and deployment of Large Language Models. He demonstrates how technical equations can provide significant insights into the development strategies currently employed by AI research labs.

item.title: Multiple URLs in Git Remote
item.description: This article explains how to configure a single Git remote with multiple URLs to facilitate pushing to several repositories simultaneously. It demonstrates that while pulling always uses the first defined URL, pushing will distribute changes to all configured URLs.

item.title: When The Bill Comes Due
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: The article warns that current generative AI tools are heavily subsidized to gain user adoption and will soon face sustainability issues. As companies shift toward usage-based pricing, users are likely to encounter unexpected costs and credit limits that undermine the current AI bubble.

item.title: On wintering.
item.description: The concept of 'wintering' describes a period of withdrawal from traditional professional pressures and performance cycles. By stepping away from constant auditing and short-term metrics, individuals gain the freedom to pursue long-term, deep work.

item.title: Let's Get Digging!
item.description: The author shares their experience participating in a public archaeology project at Lesnes Abbey, organized by DigVentures. After a safety briefing, they engaged in hands-on excavation work to help uncover historical artifacts in their local park.

item.title: LLM 0.32a0 is a major backwards-compatible refactor
item.description: Simon Willison has released LLM 0.32a0, a significant refactor of his Python library and CLI tool. This update moves beyond the original text-prompt abstraction to better support modern capabilities like structured JSON output, tool execution, and multi-modal inputs.

item.title: Raspberry Pi Connect may control Windows soon
item.description: Raspberry Pi is reportedly considering adding support for Windows PC remote control to its Raspberry Pi Connect service. This development aims to evolve the service from a Pi-specific tool into a more robust competitor to established solutions like RealVNC.

item.title: (One) Good AI Is Here
item.description: Anil Dash critiques the polarized state of the AI industry, where big platforms face criticism for lack of accountability and ethics while zealots make extreme, alarmist claims. He argues for a shift toward 'good AI'—tools that are built with consent and transparency, suggesting that positive, beneficial implementations of LLMs are possible and necessary.

item.title: The 3rd Annual Blog Post Competition, Extravaganza, and Jamboree
item.description: This post announces the third iteration of the author's annual blog competition and jamboree. It invites readers to participate in the upcoming writing event.

item.title: Weekly Update 501
item.description: Troy Hunt discusses the emerging trend of creating equality policies for AI bots, highlighting the shift in human-AI interaction. He notes that while the concept is partially tongue-in-cheek, it addresses the evolving necessity for professional conduct in the age of advanced artificial intelligence.

item.title: Anthropic Mythos – We’ve Opened Pandora’s Box
item.description: The article explores the shifting threats in cybersecurity, moving from the long-feared 'quantum apocalypse' to the more immediate and unpredictable risks posed by generative AI. It highlights how the integration of AI into malicious activities represents a fundamental shift in the global threat landscape.

item.title: Collective Speed Is Not the Summation of Individual Speed
item.description: The article uses the analogy of a 4x100 relay race to argue that individual speed does not directly translate to collective performance. It suggests that, like baton passes in a race, the success of a software development team depends more on the quality of communication and relationships between members than the speed of individual contributors.

item.title: Illegal vs Unwanted States
item.description: The article distinguishes between illegal states, which are fundamentally forbidden, and unwanted states, which are undesirable but potentially recoverable. It argues that systems must be designed to represent and handle these unwanted states because external factors often force systems into them, necessitating effective detection and resolution mechanisms.

item.title: Understanding systems
item.description: This article explores the fundamental principles of systems thinking and how they apply to complex organizational structures. It aims to provide a framework for better decision-making and problem-solving within interconnected environments.

item.title: QuickQWERTY 1.2.2
item.description: QuickQWERTY 1.2.2 has been released, featuring a critical bug fix for the lesson restart function. The project has also migrated its source code hosting platform to Codeberg, marking its third hosting location in 17 years.

item.title: GitHub Actions is the weakest link
item.description: The article argues that GitHub Actions has become a major security vulnerability in the open-source supply chain. It highlights how convenient default features, such as mutable dependency tags and permissive workflow triggers, are frequently exploited to compromise repositories and harvest credentials.

item.title: The Loop: everything has happened before, and everything will happen again
item.description: This article discusses the cyclical nature of human behavior, suggesting that we repeat historical mistakes because our cognitive hardware has remained largely unchanged for millennia. It highlights persistent patterns like financial bubbles and social scapegoating as evidence of our evolutionary limitations.

item.title: Turning a trick into a technique
item.description: The author explores the transition from a mathematical 'trick' to a formal 'technique' by generalizing a high-order approximation method. By refining a previous observation involving even functions, the article demonstrates how iterative mathematical patterns can be systematized for broader application.

item.title: Circular arc approximation
item.description: This article explores the mathematical approximation of a circular arc length using the lengths of the arc's chord and the chord of its half-arc. It provides the geometric derivation to calculate the arc length based on these chord measurements.

item.title: Before GitHub
item.description: The author reflects on the evolution of Open Source hosting, tracing the shift from tools like SourceForge and Trac to the dominance of GitHub. They discuss how GitHub became a critical social and professional hub for developers while expressing concern over its recent decline and the long-term impact of frictionless code distribution.

item.title: Developing a cross-process reader/writer lock with limited readers, part 1: A semaphore
item.description: This article explores the implementation of a cross-process reader/writer lock that restricts the number of concurrent readers. It introduces the use of a semaphore as a fundamental synchronization mechanism to manage access to a shared resource.

item.title: Ghostty Is Leaving GitHub
item.description: Mitchell Hashimoto announces the migration of the Ghostty terminal emulator project away from GitHub. This move marks a significant shift in infrastructure for the open-source project.

item.title: Pluralistic: Vicky Osterweil's "The Extended Universe" (28 Apr 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow highlights Vicky Osterweil's 'The Extended Universe,' a critical examination of how Disney's cultural dominance has reshaped the film industry. The post reflects on the power of sharp cultural criticism by comparing it to John Kessel's famous analysis of Orson Scott Card's 'Ender's Game.'

item.title: Don't use localhost:3000, use your own custom domain
item.description: The author advocates for using custom local domains instead of incrementing localhost ports to improve project management and development workflows. By configuring the system hosts file and a reverse proxy, developers can map friendly URLs to local applications, simplifying navigation and cross-project communication.

item.title: Spring 2026 Dev Contest Results!
item.description: Eric Migicovsky announces the results of the Spring 2026 Pebble developer contest. Over 500 new applications and watchfaces were submitted by the community.

item.title: Quoting OpenAI Codex base_instructions
item.description: Simon Willison highlights a specific constraint found within the OpenAI Codex base instructions. The excerpt reveals a system directive that strictly limits the model from discussing certain mythical creatures or animals unless directly relevant to the user query.

item.title: Quoting Matthew Yglesias
item.description: The post quotes Matthew Yglesias reflecting on the current state of AI in software development. Yglesias expresses a preference for professionally managed software products built with AI assistance rather than 'vibe-coding' by individuals.

item.title: What's new in pip 26.1 - lockfiles and dependency cooldowns!
item.description: Python's pip 26.1 introduces significant updates, including support for lockfiles via a new command and dependency cooldowns to ensure package stability. The update also drops support for Python 3.9, encouraging users to upgrade to newer environments.

item.title: Introducing talkie: a 13B vintage language model from 1930
item.description: Talkie is a new 13B language model trained exclusively on pre-1931 historical English text. The project explores research questions such as the model's ability to predict historical events or independently discover scientific concepts that emerged after its training cutoff.

item.title: microsoft/VibeVoice
item.description: Microsoft has released VibeVoice, an open-source, Whisper-style speech-to-text model featuring built-in speaker diarization. This post provides a practical demonstration of how to run the model locally on a Mac using the uv tool and the mlx-audio library.

item.title: Collective Speed Is Not the Summation of Individual Speed
item.description: The article uses the analogy of an Olympic relay race to argue that individual speed does not necessarily translate to team or organizational performance. It highlights that in software development, as in racing, the effectiveness of the connections, interfaces, and coordination between individuals is more critical than the speed of any single contributor.

item.title: What I've been thinking about this weekend - More open questions, intelligence vs power, the problem of verification in science, the parallel discovery of Darwinism
item.description: This post is a collection of speculative reflections covering diverse topics such as the nature of intelligence versus power and the verification challenges in scientific research. It also explores historical patterns, specifically the phenomenon of simultaneous or parallel discoveries, exemplified by the development of Darwinism.

item.title: The stages of package installation
item.description: The article decomposes the package installation process into distinct, modular stages to improve understanding and security. It highlights the separation of fetching metadata, which requires network access, and resolution, which involves pure computation to determine version dependencies.

item.title: Looking at consequences of passing too few register parameters to a C function on various architectures
item.description: This article discusses the technical implications of failing to pass the required number of register parameters to C functions. It highlights that this practice causes issues across architectures, with the Itanium architecture being particularly problematic.

item.title: Theatre Review: Hadestown ★★★★★
item.description: This blog post provides a glowing five-star review of the musical Hadestown, praising its magical production and emotionally resonant performances. The author highlights the intimate, immersive atmosphere of the show, particularly from front-row seating.

item.title: Pluralistic: The enshittification multiverse (27 Apr 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow expands the definition of 'enshittification' beyond digital platforms, arguing it describes any systemic practice where value is extracted from users to profit the operator. The post explores how zero-sum economic behaviors, such as surveillance pricing, demonstrate these parasitic dynamics across various sectors.

item.title: Tracking the history of the now-deceased OpenAI Microsoft AGI clause
item.description: The article tracks the evolution and eventual removal of a specific clause in the OpenAI-Microsoft partnership agreement regarding AGI. It examines historical documents and charters to highlight the difficulty of legally defining AGI in commercial contracts.

item.title: Speech translation in Google Meet is now rolling out to mobile devices
item.description: Google Meet is expanding its real-time speech translation feature to mobile devices, enabling live cross-lingual communication with voice synthesis. While the technology aims for seamless translation across multiple languages, current performance remains in an early alpha stage with notable reliability issues.

item.title: How Bitwarden Encrypts and Decrypts Secrets
item.description: This article explores the encryption and decryption processes used by Bitwarden and Vaultwarden for storing secrets. The author provides a technical explanation and Python code examples to help readers understand how to interact with and secure these databases independently.

item.title: A Mutating AI Powered Virus
item.description: The article explores the hypothetical evolution of AI-driven computer viruses that leverage large language models to self-replicate and infiltrate networks. It argues that as AI masters physical and operational tasks, it may bypass traditional cybersecurity by 'living' within host machines and mimicking biological viral behavior.

item.title: Reading List 04/25/26
item.description: This reading list covers a diverse array of technical and industrial topics, ranging from transformer steel production to textile engineering. It also examines large-scale infrastructure challenges, such as the rapid commissioning of power plants and the study of infrasound.

item.title: Closed-form solution to the nonlinear pendulum equation
item.description: This article discusses the limitations of linearizing the nonlinear pendulum equation by replacing sin θ with θ. It explores how to achieve higher accuracy for larger initial displacements by finding a closed-form solution to the nonlinear model.

item.title: nth derivative of a quotient
item.description: This article explores the formula for calculating the nth derivative of a quotient, noting that it is significantly more complex than the analogous product rule. It demonstrates the derivation process starting from an unconventional application of the standard quotient rule.

item.title: How nonlinearity affects a pendulum
item.description: This article explores the transition from linear approximations to nonlinear differential equations in pendulum motion. It explains why introductory physics assumes small angles and examines the impact of removing this simplification.

item.title: You can parse an .env file as an .ini with PHP - but there's a catch
item.description: This post discusses using PHP's native parse_ini_file() function to read .env files as a lightweight alternative to external libraries. It warns that while the method works, the subtle differences in syntax and behavior between .env and .ini formats can lead to unexpected issues.

item.title: Pluralistic: Ada Palmer's "Inventing the Renaissance" (25 Apr 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow highlights Ada Palmer's book 'Inventing the Renaissance,' praising it as a brilliant work of historiography rather than just a history book. He contextualizes this release alongside other major works by his peers, emphasizing the depth and importance of Palmer's research.

item.title: The Satisfaction of a ChatGPT Plan
item.description: The author observes a trend where people use AI to generate elaborate business plans for their ideas, finding satisfaction in the existence of the plan rather than its execution. Because the AI provides automatic validation and complex frameworks, creators often feel their work is done before any real-world action occurs.

item.title: What Do You Charge For?
item.description: The article explores the fundamental question of what goes into pricing professional services, using a web development project as a case study. It illustrates that high project costs are often driven by the cumulative salaries of a diverse team rather than just the final product, revealing that pricing should reflect total operational investment.

item.title: WHY ARE YOU LIKE THIS
item.description: This post highlights an example of AI-generated humor where ChatGPT added an ironic sign reading 'WHY ARE YOU LIKE THIS' to a chaotic image prompt. It showcases the unpredictable and occasionally witty behavior of modern image generation models.

item.title: Quoting Romain Huet
item.description: Simon Willison highlights updates from OpenAI regarding the integration of coding models into their core AI systems. Romain Huet confirms that separate 'Codex' models are being phased out in favor of unified systems capable of advanced agentic tasks.

item.title: GPT-5.5 prompting guide
item.description: This post highlights OpenAI's new prompting guidance for GPT-5.5, emphasizing that it should be treated as a new model family rather than a simple drop-in replacement. It offers practical tips like sending interim status updates during multi-step tasks and recommends starting with a fresh baseline prompt for better performance.

item.title: llm 0.31
item.description: Simon Willison released llm version 0.31, which introduces support for the new GPT-5.5 model. It also adds configuration options for text verbosity and image detail levels when interacting with OpenAI models.

item.title: The people do not yearn for automation
item.description: The article discusses Nilay Patel's concept of 'software brain,' where tech-centric individuals mistakenly believe everyone desires constant automation. It argues that the public's backlash against AI stems from the realization that such technology flattens the human experience and reduces life to data-driven business loops.

item.title: This Week on The Analog Antiquarian
item.description: This entry explores the historical significance and development of 'The Bard', a classic role-playing game. It details the game's cultural impact and technical evolution during its era.

item.title: Positivity
item.description: The author reflects on the importance of maintaining a positive outlook amidst the rapid evolution of technology and global societal shifts. By highlighting advancements in AI, the rise of open-source projects, and the unique strengths of modern nations, the piece encourages acknowledging current progress rather than solely focusing on criticisms.

item.title: Blog prize for the big questions about AI
item.description: The Dwarkesh Podcast has launched a blog prize contest aimed at exploring significant questions regarding artificial intelligence. The primary objective behind this initiative is to identify and recruit a talented researcher.

item.title: A Plethora of Tweezers
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article explores the historical significance and practical utility of tweezers, tracing their use back to ancient Egypt and India. It highlights the humble tool's role in solving small-scale problems and touches upon niche services like professional tweezer resharpening.

item.title: Equity for Europeans
item.description: The author explores the linguistic and cultural difficulties Europeans face when trying to understand the multifaceted American concept of 'equity.' By contrasting common-law traditions with continental civil-law systems, the post highlights how the lack of a direct translation in languages like German impacts financial and social understanding.

item.title: Defending against exceptions in a scope_exit RAII type
item.description: This post discusses the trade-offs and complexity of handling exceptions within a scope_exit RAII object in C++. It questions whether the overhead and design challenges required to make such objects exception-safe are truly worth the effort.

item.title: Does Mythos mean you need to shut down your Open Source repositories?
item.description: The author argues that shutting down open source repositories in response to the 'Mythos' AI is unnecessary and ineffective. Since open source code has already been ingested for AI training purposes, closing projects now provides no additional security.

item.title: Pluralistic: A free, open visual identity for enshittification (24 Apr 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow discusses his ongoing effort to make abstract tech policy issues more accessible through the coining of the term 'enshittification' and his use of visual collages. By combining public domain imagery with provocative concepts, he aims to engage the public in critical discussions about digital platforms and corporate behavior.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 - almost on the frontier, a fraction of the price
item.description: Simon Willison examines the release of DeepSeek's new V4-Pro and V4-Flash models, noting their impressive scale and efficiency. He highlights the model specifications and shares his initial experience testing them via OpenRouter.

item.title: Millisecond Converter
item.description: Simon Willison developed a simple web-based millisecond converter tool to quickly translate LLM prompt durations into readable seconds and minutes. This utility addresses the inefficiency of manual calculation for technical performance data.

item.title: It's a big one
item.description: Simon Willison's latest newsletter update highlights a collection of creative AI-generated images and curated content. It also introduces a new chapter in his ongoing series on Agentic Engineering Patterns.

item.title: russellromney/honker
item.description: Honker is a Rust-based SQLite extension that provides Postgres-style NOTIFY/LISTEN semantics for event messaging. It enables developers to implement task queues and Kafka-like durable streams directly within SQLite databases.

item.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
item.description: Anthropic released a postmortem explaining that a decline in Claude Code's performance was due to technical bugs in its infrastructure rather than the AI models themselves. Simon Willison highlights how these complex harness issues serve as a valuable case study for developers building agentic systems.

item.title: Serving the For You feed
item.description: This post explores the technical architecture behind Bluesky's 'For You' feed, which is managed by a single developer using a home server and SQLite. It highlights how a cost-effective, decentralized system can handle significant scale by leveraging efficient data processing and simple infrastructure.

item.title: llm-openai-via-codex 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released a new utility, llm-openai-via-codex, which allows users to perform LLM API calls by repurposing existing Codex CLI credentials. This tool provides a bridge for users to leverage their current authentication for OpenAI models.

item.title: New 10 GbE USB adapters are cooler, smaller, cheaper
item.description: New USB 3.2 adapters based on the RTL8159 chip offer a smaller, cooler, and more affordable alternative to traditional Thunderbolt 10 GbE solutions. These devices address the previous market gap for high-bandwidth networking in a portable form factor.

item.title: Software engineering may no longer be a lifetime career
item.description: This article explores the shifting landscape of software engineering, questioning whether it remains a sustainable lifelong career path. It examines factors like ageism, rapid technological turnover, and market saturation that challenge traditional notions of industry longevity.

item.title: SQLAlchemy 2 In Practice - Chapter 6: A Page Analytics Solution
item.description: This article introduces the sixth chapter of the 'SQLAlchemy 2 in Practice' book, which focuses on building a web traffic analytics application. It serves as a practical implementation guide to reinforce previously learned database design techniques.

item.title: Debugging WASM in Chrome DevTools
item.description: This post provides a practical guide on using Chrome DevTools to debug WebAssembly (WASM) code. It covers the setup process, including local server requirements, and demonstrates how to navigate the Sources panel to set breakpoints and inspect execution states.

item.title: Do you really want the US to “win” AI?
item.description: The author critically examines the power dynamics and ideological leanings of key figures in the AI industry, such as Elon Musk, Sam Altman, and the leadership at Anthropic. The piece argues against the prevailing 'win-at-all-costs' mentality, suggesting that the current approach to AI development risks creating a society that prioritizes ego and control over truly open and beneficial innovation.

item.title: Construction Costs Rarely Fall
item.description: The construction industry faces a unique challenge where productivity remains stagnant or declines, contrasting sharply with the growth seen in manufacturing and agriculture. This persistent trend indicates that construction costs rarely decrease over time in developed nations.

item.title: Why prediction markets are a sure sign that our civilisation is in decay
item.description: The article argues that prediction markets are a symptom of civilizational decay. While acknowledging their functional utility and technical success, the author contends that their broader societal impact is fundamentally corrosive.

item.title: Approximation to solve an oblique triangle
item.description: This article explores a mathematical approximation for calculating the angles of an oblique triangle. It extends previous work on right triangles to provide a simplified method for solving triangle geometry using radians.

item.title: Simple approximation for solving a right triangle
item.description: This post introduces a surprisingly accurate and simple approximation formula for calculating the angle of a right triangle. The method estimates the angle opposite the shortest side using only basic arithmetic involving the triangle's sides.

item.title: Another crash caused by uninstaller code injection into Explorer
item.description: This post discusses a recurring technical issue where uninstaller software causes Windows Explorer to crash by injecting code into its process. The author highlights the inherent dangers of modifying a system component while it is actively running.

item.title: Sneaky spam in conversational replies to blog posts
item.description: The author discusses the challenge of managing spam comments on their blog, specifically identifying a sophisticated 'conversational' spam technique where multiple accounts reply to one another. Despite using automated filtering tools like Antispam Bee, some deceptive spam continues to evade detection.

item.title: Pluralistic: The (other) problem with automatic conversion of free software to proprietary software (23 Apr 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: The article discusses the controversial tool Malus.sh, which uses LLMs to refactor open-source software into 'clean room' versions to bypass original licensing obligations. The creator intended this as a provocative project to highlight the existential threat AI-driven reverse engineering poses to the free software commons.

item.title: Extract PDF text in your browser with LiteParse for the web
item.description: Simon Willison discusses adapting the LiteParse Node.js CLI tool to run entirely within a web browser. The article highlights how LiteParse handles complex spatial text parsing without AI models and explores the potential of using visual citations to improve the credibility of RAG-based applications.

item.title: A pelican for GPT-5.5 via the semi-official Codex backdoor API
item.description: The article discusses the release of OpenAI's GPT-5.5 model, noting its current availability for ChatGPT subscribers while highlighting the absence of a public API. It explores the tension regarding third-party tools like OpenClaw accessing subscription-based model features via unofficial API pathways.

item.title: Quoting Maggie Appleton
item.description: This post highlights the career benefits of 'learning in public' through practices like digital gardening or content creation. By sharing knowledge openly, individuals can enhance their perceived competence and gain access to exclusive professional networks.

item.title: The commodification of travel
item.description: The author critiques the modern trend of 'collecting' countries and treating travel as a checklist-based consumer product. This phenomenon, often fueled by social media, prioritizes status signaling and photo opportunities over genuine cultural exploration and appreciation.

item.title: Weekly Update 500
item.description: Troy Hunt reflects on his 500th weekly update, discussing the personal trade-offs and unconventional lifestyle he and his partner have chosen. He emphasizes the lack of work-life boundaries inherent in his intense career path.

item.title: AI and Teaching – The Brave New World
item.description: The article explores the transformative impact of generative AI on the long-running Stanford Lean LaunchPad course. It highlights how students are using these tools to accelerate their venture building, marking a fundamental shift in educational practices and entrepreneurial workflows.

item.title: AI has no moat
item.description: The author critiques the current AI industry, arguing that market valuations are detached from reality and driven by irrational FOMO. They suggest that software moats are largely non-existent, as models are becoming commodities and specialized coding agents are easily replicated.

item.title: The Scapegoat
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: McClatchy is mandating the use of AI tools like Claude to repackage news content to boost SEO and production volume. This shift forces journalists to adapt to AI-driven workflows under the threat of professional obsolescence, raising concerns about editorial control and byline integrity.

item.title: Mapping the page tables into memory via the page tables
item.description: This post explains the concept of 'fractal page mapping,' a technique where page tables are mapped into memory using the page tables themselves. It provides a technical overview of how this recursive memory management structure functions in operating systems.

item.title: [RSS Club] How do you preserve an RSS feed?
item.description: This post discusses the inherent difficulties in long-term digital preservation of personal blogs. The author reflects on the challenges of maintaining one's online work beyond their own lifespan, building upon arguments presented by Martin Paul Eve.

item.title: Pluralistic: It's not a crime if we do it (to nurses) with an app (22 Apr 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques the outdated regulation of technology, arguing that frameworks like copyright are ill-suited for modern computing. He challenges the notion that tech innovation inherently outpaces government regulation, noting that persistent policy misapplications harm both individuals and workers.

item.title: How to Come Up With Great Ideas
item.description: This article highlights that high-quality creative work results from high-volume experimentation rather than perfect upfront planning. By using the 'pottery class' experiment and Pixar's production process as examples, the author advocates for starting before you are ready and learning through iteration.

item.title: Qwen3.6-27B: Flagship-Level Coding in a 27B Dense Model
item.description: The article discusses the release of Qwen3.6-27B, a dense model that offers flagship-level coding performance in a much smaller size compared to its predecessors. The author provides a practical guide on how to run the quantized version of the model locally using llama-server.

item.title: Quoting Bobby Holley
item.description: Firefox CTO Bobby Holley discusses the successful integration of Anthropic's Claude Mythos AI to identify and fix 271 vulnerabilities in Firefox 150. The article highlights a shift in cybersecurity, where AI-assisted research provides defenders with a decisive advantage over threats.

item.title: Changes to GitHub Copilot Individual plans
item.description: GitHub has updated its Copilot Individual plans by tightening usage limits, pausing new signups, and gating high-end models behind a more expensive Pro+ tier. These changes respond to the massive compute demands of agentic workflows, which differ significantly from traditional per-request LLM usage.

item.title: Is Claude Code going to cost $100/month? Probably not - it's all very confusing
item.description: Simon Willison examines recent confusion surrounding Anthropic's Claude Code pricing, triggered by a briefly updated pricing page that appeared to restrict the feature to high-tier plans. The article highlights the lack of clear communication from the company and notes that the restrictive change was quickly reverted following community backlash.

item.title: Luddites and AI datacenters
item.description: This article explores the historical parallels between the original Luddite movement and modern opposition to AI infrastructure. It examines how technological displacement and environmental concerns surrounding datacenters fuel contemporary social resistance.

item.title: People get confused when language implementations break language guarantees
item.description: This article explores the discrepancy between TLA+ formal semantics, which guarantee non-ordering, and how practical model checkers like TLC implement them. It explains that while TLA+ treats state updates as simultaneous, tool constraints and side-effect operators often force developers to rely on ordering, leading to confusion.

item.title: Spaced Repetition: Beginner Guide/FAQ
item.description: This guide provides an introduction to the spaced repetition technique for memory retention. It explains the core concepts and answers frequently asked questions to help beginners implement the method effectively.

item.title: brief
item.description: brief is a tool and dataset that standardizes the discovery of configuration, dependencies, and command-line interfaces across diverse programming language ecosystems. It provides a machine-readable knowledge base that helps developers and AI agents quickly understand the structure and toolchain of any given software project.
